title: Client update: LLM output drift — verification kit and status
content:
TL;DR
On 2028-03-02 we observed a change in output characteristics (semantic drift) for one of our hosted model variants that caused a subset of API responses to deviate from expected formats/tones for ~90 minutes. We mitigated by routing affected traffic to a pinned model variant and rolling a targeted rollback for the model runtime configuration. Customers may have seen: subtle content shifts, changed score ordering for reranking, or truncated structured outputs. No customer data was exposed.

What we are sharing in this doc
- A plain-language status brief suitable for posting to status.redwood.ai (short).
- A customer-facing post-incident summary (concise) that explains cause and remedies.
- A small verification checklist customers can run to validate their recent requests (self-serve).
- Recommendations and next steps if customers want additional evidence or replay.
- Links to operator artifacts (Jira/Confluence) for customers with contractual audit needs.

Audience
Primary: engineering contacts at affected customers, platform/security reviewers, partner integrations team. Secondary: product and SRE stakeholders.

SHORT STATUS SNIPPET (for statuspage)
Title: Deviation in model outputs affecting a subset of responses — mitigated
Status: Major Incident — Mitigated
Summary: Between 22:10 UTC and 23:40 UTC on 2028-03-02 we observed anomalous output drift for a hosted model variant. We have routed traffic to a pinned model variant and deployed a rollback of the runtime config. Customers may notice minor differences in conversational tone, ranking order, or structured field content for affected requests during that window. No data leak or credential exposure. Full customer postmortem will be posted once final verification completes.

WHO SAW IMPACT
- A traffic slice (~2.7% of requests) routed to the newest model runtime variant in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 during the specified window.
- Impacted APIs: text generation, chat completions, and ranking endpoints that used model alias: redwood-open-v5-dyn
- Typical customer symptom: outputs that were syntactically valid but semantically shifted (e.g., different tone, re-ordered lists, missing optional fields in structured JSON output).

IMPACT SUMMARY
- Functional correctness: transient regression in output expectations for affected requests.
- Latency: unchanged.
- Data security: none — no external exfiltration or unauthorized access detected.
- Billing/SLAs: small fraction of requests impacted; we are evaluating SLA credit eligibility per contracts — contact your account team if you want expedited review.

TIMELINE (high level)
- 2028-03-02 22:08 UTC — anomalous drift alerts triggered by our synthetic evals and customer anomaly detector (rank-stability monitors).
- 2028-03-02 22:10 UTC — Ops engaged; first customer reports arrive via support.
- 2028-03-02 22:25 UTC — Identified correlation with a runtime config rollout that changed the kernel selection heuristics for long-context softmax.
- 2028-03-02 22:40 UTC — Applied immediate traffic steering to pinned stable variant for all Tier 1 customers.
- 2028-03-02 23:00 UTC — Scoped rollback of runtime config to prior stable build in eu-west-1; began global rollback.
- 2028-03-02 23:20 UTC — Observability shows outputs returning to baseline distributions.
- 2028-03-02 23:40 UTC — Incident declared mitigated; monitoring elevated for 48 hours.

ROOT CAUSE (concise)
A binary rollout of a runtime optimization intended to improve kernel selection for long-context models introduced a subtle numerical change in softmax scaling for one model architecture on certain sequences. That numerical shift affected probability distributions at token-selection time, which manifested as semantic drift for some prompts. The change passed normal unit/integration tests but was not covered by the synthetic eval set for the affected prompt family.

WHAT WE DID (mitigation + remediation)
Immediate actions (during the incident)
- Re-routed traffic to a pinned stable model variant for affected customers and regions.
- Rolled back the runtime optimization flag to the prior value.
- Brought forward an expanded synthetic evaluation run that includes the failing prompt family.
- Notified impacted customers and set up private channels for evidence verification on request.

Post-incident follow-ups (next 30 days)
- Expand synthetic eval set and add adversarial prompt coverage for the affected prompt patterns.
- Add a numeric-sensitivity gate to kernel selection changes (automated check that flags X% distribution shifts on held-out prompt family).
- Update release checklist to require A/B sample checking for any softmax or sampling-related change.
- Longer term: instrument per-tenant profile drift alerts so we can detect tenant-specific sensitivity earlier.

Customer verification kit (recommended steps to reproduce/validate)
If you want to confirm whether your requests were impacted during the window, please follow the checklist below. These are quick steps your engineers can run and share results if you need help.
1) Identify candidate timestamps in your logs between 2028-03-02 22:10 UTC and 2028-03-02 23:40 UTC.
2) For a small sample (5–20) of requests: record the request payload, model alias used (if present), and full response from your logs.
3) Re-run the recorded request payloads against the pinned stable model variant (alias: redwood-open-v5-stable) using the same API parameters (temperature, max_tokens, sampling args). Note: this is a read-only verification — no changes to your integration required.
4) Compare outputs for qualitative differences: tone, list ordering, presence/absence of expected structured fields. If you used deterministic sampling (temperature=0), compare exact token sequences.
5) If you observe a significant difference, collect 3–5 examples and open a support ticket with evidence; include request_id, timestamps, and raw logs.

If you do not want to run checks yourself
- Contact support and we will run a scoped evidence package for you (we will need consent to access the specific request logs).

Evidence we can provide on request
- Redacted request/response pairs (we will redact tenant-sensitive fields if needed).
- Server-side trace showing model alias and kernel config at the time of processing.
- Synthetic-eval delta report used to verify rollout impact.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (concise)
We take model output stability seriously. On 2028-03-02 a runtime rollout changed the numerical behavior of token-selection for a small share of requests, which caused semantic shifts in some outputs. We mitigated by pinning traffic to a stable model and rolling back the runtime change. We are adding additional synthetic and adversarial checks to our deployment gating and will follow up with a technical appendix if you require deeper evidence. If you believe you were materially affected (e.g., user-facing regressions, compliance exposures, or billing disputes), please reach out to your account rep or open a priority support ticket.

Compensation / SLA note
If you experienced measurable degradation tied to business impact, we will evaluate SLA credit per your contract terms. Please engage your account team with a short summary of the impact window and estimated business effect; we will triage accordingly.

Frequently asked questions (quick)
Q: Was any customer data exposed?
A: No. This was a numeric/runtime change; no data exfiltration or unauthorized access occurred.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We have short-term mitigations (synthetic expansion, numeric-sensitivity gate) and a longer-term plan to instrument per-tenant drift. Residual risk will be lower; we will continue to harden release controls for sampling/softmax changes.

Q: Do I need to change my integration?
A: No. No API changes are required. If you rely on deterministic sampling, you can validate by re-running sample requests with temperature=0.

How to escalate / get help
- Open a support ticket and select Priority: High, subject: "LLM output drift verification" — include request_ids and timestamps.
- If you have an account rep, email them directly and we will assemble an evidence package.
- For enterprise customers requiring an audit artifact, we can provide a redacted evidence bundle and an operator timeline.

Notes to internal ops (quick)
- Add INF-1129 follow-up to next on-call rotation: add numeric-sensitivity check to gating.
- Product to schedule synthetic expansion: OWNER: Owen Martinez; ETA: 2028-03-18.
- SRE to include per-tenant drift alert POC in Q2 roadmap.

Appendix: sample support ticket template (copy to paste)
Subject: Verification request — LLMD drift (2028-03-02 22:10–23:40 UTC)
Body: Hi Support — Please run a scoped verification for tenant <TENANT-ID>. Affected window: 2028-03-02 22:10–23:40 UTC. Example request_ids: <id1>, <id2>, <id3>. We consent to Redwood accessing request logs for evidence. Please return redacted request/response pairs and server-side kernel config for those requests.

End of doc — draft for customer review.
(Notes: keep short status snip for statuspage and send the verification kit as a private attachment to affected customers. Lean on product to provide the synthetic delta CSV for enterprise audit requests.)
